request: Hi , Please change the center flower type profile into a hexagonal profile for better torque transfer

actions.operation: Replace the existing center flower-type profile with a hexagonal profile.
actions.relational_constraint: The hexagonal profile must replace the referenced flower-type profile at the same central location.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the center flower-type profile in the original CAD model and determine its existing extent and associated feature definition.
steps: Localize the requested flower-type geometry at the model center using the +Z/front and iso1 views. It is the visibly six-lobed external profile of the separate splined hub insert, not the fine internal spline opening and not the 27-tooth outer sprocket rim.

Modify section R01, the separate splined hub insert in SOLID 0. Treat F001 as the parent insert-body feature. FACE 1 is the principal front annular face whose boundary participates in the visible flower-shaped region; the associated secondary insert transition walls are contained within FACE 225 through FACE 232.

Also modify the corresponding mating recess in section R02 so the carrier remains compatible with the revised insert. Use F009 as the receiving-interface feature and FACE 496 as the carrier front reference face. Identify the flower-recess wall subset adjoining the central opening from the central support and transition surfaces grouped within FACE 497 through FACE 667.

Preserve F002 and its internal spline geometry, including representative tooth flanks FACE 3 and FACE 4 and the repeated spline faces through FACE 223. The request concerns the external flower-shaped insert-to-carrier drive profile; removing the internal shaft spline would alter a separate functional interface.

Establish a sketch plane perpendicular to the common rotational axis of F001 and F009, using the plane of FACE 1 for the insert-side profile. Project the model axis and the existing flower-profile envelope into the sketch to maintain exact concentricity.

Measure the existing flower profile's maximum radial envelope, minimum wall thickness to the internal spline, axial engagement depth, and mating clearance. Use those values to size the replacement regular hexagon; no unsupported across-flats or across-corners dimension is to be introduced.

Sketch a fully constrained regular six-sided polygon centered on the existing rotational axis. Constrain its size so that it remains within the available insert envelope and preserves adequate material between the hex flats or corners and the internal spline roots. Constrain its angular orientation to an existing model datum or to the symmetry orientation of the original six-lobed profile.

Remove or suppress the insert's existing six-lobed flower-profile definition and its associated lobe transition surfaces. Rebuild the affected portion of SOLID 0 with the hexagonal external profile over the same axial engagement depth as the original flower-shaped interface, while retaining the rear cylindrical locating seat FACE 2 and the unaffected axial support geometry.

On the carrier front reference plane at FACE 496, project or derive the new insert hexagon and apply the required assembly clearance based on the original flower-interface fit. Create a matching concentric hexagonal pocket in the carrier receiving region without changing the cylindrical locating function of FACE 669 unless the original flower profile extends through that cylindrical seat.

Extrude-cut the carrier hexagonal pocket to the exact depth of the original flower-shaped recess. Terminate the cut at the existing internal shoulder or use the original flower-pocket terminal face as the up-to-face limit so the insert's axial seating position is unchanged.

Where required for assembly, reproduce the existing entry treatment with a small lead-in chamfer on the exposed hexagonal edges. Keep the chamfer subordinate to the torque-bearing flat area, and do not apply fillets to the primary hex flats unless required by the mating-part manufacturing process.

Check that the revised insert and carrier remain separate solids, SOLID 0 and SOLID 1, and that the hexagonal profiles are concentric, angularly aligned, and clearance-compatible. Confirm that the insert axial seating faces remain coincident with their original assembly positions.

Validate that the new hex flats provide positive torque-bearing contact between R01 and R02, that the internal spline F002 remains unobstructed through the full 7.8 mm insert axial extent, and that no interference is introduced into the spoke-web body or central receiving bore.

Regenerate the model and inspect the +Z/front, -Z/back, axial side, and isometric views. The former six-lobed center outline should be replaced by a regular hexagonal interface while the internal spline, carrier spokes, lightening cutouts, and outer sprocket teeth remain unchanged.
